messages.Above the player, activate Combine varia: Above the player, activate Combine variables. Choose the records to include with the checkboxes. Each map card has its record switch and readings. Muted maps stay visible in gray. Playback and place controls still apply. Activate One variable to return to an individual variable.
messages.Without a regional selection, readings s: Without a regional selection, readings summarize decoded pixels across the image. Select a region or country to focus the map and switch both readings and sound to that region. Pixel inclusion shows the share of analyzed image pixels used, not accuracy or geographic surface area.
messages.Python converts image colors to the near: Python converts image colors to the nearest value in the visualization legend. Logos and timestamps are excluded. Regional estimates use pixel centers inside the selected boundaries; country groups follow whole-country assignments and contain land territories, not surrounding oceans. Europe includes all Russia; Asia excludes Russia.
messages.P90 is the unweighted 90th percentile of: P90 is the unweighted 90th percentile of decoded pixel values, not a confidence level. These remain image-derived estimates; weighting cannot reconstruct missing or rejected pixels and does not make them direct numerical GEOS-FP fields.
messages.Pixel inclusion = pixels used ÷ analyzed: Pixel inclusion = pixels used ÷ analyzed pixels after excluding overlays. It does not measure scientific accuracy, instrument reliability or geographic surface area. Missing inclusion is unavailable, not zero; 100% inclusion does not establish accuracy.
messages.Python computes norm = (mean − legend mi: Python computes norm = (mean − legend minimum) ÷ (legend maximum − legend minimum), limited to 0–1 and rounded to three decimals. It is a position on the fixed legend scale, not a percentile or a percentage of Earth. The front displays the supplied values. Temperature, carbon monoxide and ozone use their supplied normalized positions for pitch. Wind and PM2.5 use the supplied visual signal index when declared. Precipitation and specific humidity use the supplied mean in their physical units.
messages.Groups follow whole-country assignments,: Groups follow whole-country assignments, not physical continental boundaries. Europe includes all of Russia; Asia excludes Russia. Oceanic island territories cover land only.
messages.Use your screen reader’s table commands: Use your screen reader’s table commands to explore cells. With spoken navigation, use Read this frame to hear only the highlighted frame.
messages.Frame readings summarize image-derived p: Frame readings summarize image-derived pixels. Coverage is the share of analyzed image pixels used, not geographic area or accuracy. Choosing a region changes the reading and sound.
messages.Mean = sum(decoded value × cosine latitu: Mean = sum(decoded value × cosine latitude) ÷ sum(cosine latitude), using accepted pixels only. P90 remains an unweighted pixel percentile. Pixel inclusion remains a pixel-count ratio, not an area percentage.
messages.This dataset uses equal weights per deco: This dataset uses equal weights per decoded pixel. P90 and coverage retain their supplied definitions.
This dataset uses equal weights per decoded pixel. Its mean has not been area-weighted.
messages.Color-filter settings unavailable; pixel: Color-filter settings unavailable; pixel inclusion does not establish measurement accuracy.
messages.No color acceptance filter is configured: No color acceptance filter is configured: each analyzed pixel is assigned its nearest legend color. 100% inclusion does not mean 100% accuracy.
messages.Mean weighted by pixel area (cosine lati: Mean weighted by pixel area (cosine latitude), over decoded pixels used
messages.Mean uses equal weights per decoded pixe: Mean uses equal weights per decoded pixel

messages.Image-derived temperature estimate decod: Image-derived temperature estimate decoded from visualization pixels. This is not a direct numerical GEOS-FP field or a complete global field. Small variations can remain on the same pentatonic note.
messages.Image-derived precipitation estimate. Co: Image-derived precipitation estimate. Colored precipitation overlays clouds and the basemap; only color-filtered pixels contribute. Coverage is the analyzed image-pixel share, not the land area receiving rain. No whole-Earth average or mm/hour conversion is assumed.
messages.Synthesized pulse · filtered single voic: Synthesized pulse · filtered single voice · lower register
messages.Carbon monoxide becomes a trumpet-like m: Carbon monoxide becomes a trumpet-like melody
messages.The supplied normalized concentration se: The supplied normalized concentration selects one note from a fixed C major pentatonic scale. Lower values sound lower; higher values sound higher. This synthetic trumpet-like tone is a data cue, not a risk alarm.
messages.Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 positio: Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 position on the fixed 40–500 ppbv legend. The selected note is not stretched to the values observed in the current frames or region.
messages.Carbon monoxide is an image-derived near: Carbon monoxide is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in ppbv, decoded from NASA SVS 5153 colors. It is not the raw numerical GEOS-CF grid. Global means change little in this interval; country and continent estimates vary more. Regional means currently use equal weights per accepted image pixel.
messages.The supplied norm selects one of 11 C ma: The supplied norm selects one of 11 C major pentatonic notes from C3 to C5. The front end does not recompute norm. Missing norm or zero pixel coverage means silence.
messages.CO values are image-derived estimates, n: CO values are image-derived estimates, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF field. Coverage is the share of analyzed image pixels used, not accuracy or geographic area. The synthetic voice does not assess health risk.
messages.A comparison of 40 and 500 ppbv legend e: A comparison of 40 and 500 ppbv legend endpoints, not the current measurements. Higher supplied concentration maps to higher pitch. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on.
messages.Lower carbon monoxide concentration mean: Lower carbon monoxide concentration means a lower trumpet-like note. Higher concentration means a higher note. This sound is not a health-risk rating.
messages.Gentle Karplus–Strong string · short pen: Gentle Karplus–Strong string · short pentatonic note per frame
messages.Ozone becomes a soft harp-like melody: Ozone becomes a soft harp-like melody
messages.The supplied normalized concentration se: The supplied normalized concentration selects one note from a fixed C major pentatonic scale. Ozone uses a higher register than the other melodic voices; higher values sound higher.
messages.Lower plucked note · C4 · 5 ppbv referen: Lower plucked note · C4 · 5 ppbv reference
messages.Higher plucked note · C6 · 60 ppbv refer: Higher plucked note · C6 · 60 ppbv reference
messages.Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 positio: Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 position on the fixed 5–60 ppbv legend. The selected note is not stretched to the values observed in the current frames or region.
messages.Ozone is an image-derived near-surface c: Ozone is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in ppbv, decoded from NASA SVS 5152 colors. It is not the raw numerical GEOS-CF grid. The global mean changes little in this interval; regional estimates vary more. Regional means currently use equal weights per accepted image pixel.
messages.The supplied norm selects one of 11 C ma: The supplied norm selects one of 11 C major pentatonic notes from C4 to C6. The front end does not recompute norm. Missing norm or zero pixel coverage means silence.
messages.Ozone values are image-derived estimates: Ozone values are image-derived estimates, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF field. About 43–46% of analyzed pixels are used in the current frames; this is image-pixel coverage, not accuracy or geographic area. The sound is not a health-risk rating.
messages.A comparison of 5 and 60 ppbv legend end: A comparison of 5 and 60 ppbv legend endpoints, not the current measurements. Higher supplied concentration maps to higher pitch. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on.
messages.Lower ozone concentration means a lower: Lower ozone concentration means a lower plucked note. Higher concentration means a higher note. This sound is not a health-risk rating.
messages.Data and frames available · sound mappin: Data and frames available · sound mapping not implemented
messages.This dataset is available for visual pla: This dataset is available for visual playback. A dedicated sound identity has not been assigned yet; it does not use the temperature instrument.
messages.The normalized value is shown as supplie: The normalized value is shown as supplied. No note or pulse rate is inferred for this experience.
messages.Read the selected dataset's measure, uni: Read the selected dataset's measure, unit and timestamp below the image. Values are derived from visualization pixels and are not automatically whole-Earth averages. Coverage describes color-filtered image pixels.
messages.The normalized value and its limits come: The normalized value and its limits come from the dataset. No sonification has been implemented for this quantity yet.
messages.Image-derived values. Use the stated dat: Image-derived values. Use the stated dataset measure and pixel coverage; no whole-Earth average or new sound mapping is assumed.
messages.Sound examples are not available for thi: Sound examples are not available for this record yet.
messages.This experience is visual only. Its dedi: This experience is visual only. Its dedicated sound mapping is not implemented yet.
messages.Visible PM2.5 patterns shape a metallic: Visible PM2.5 patterns shape a metallic shimmer
More intense and extensive detected PM2.5 colors produce a higher, brighter metallic tone. A rising tone follows an increase in visible signal; a falling tone follows a decrease. Loudness stays fixed.
messages.The same 0–1 visual index and pitch curv: The same 0–1 visual index and pitch curve apply to every country, group and frame. Regions are not stretched separately: their tones can be compared directly.
messages.The visual index combines log-scaled col: The visual index combines log-scaled color intensity with its area-weighted extent. It supports comparisons of more versus less signal. The concentration mean in µg/m³ remains a separate diagnostic; the index is not a concentration or health rating.
messages.Sound uses the supplied visual index dir: Sound uses the supplied visual index directly. Higher indices always produce higher, brighter sustained tones on the same fixed curve. No detected pixels means unavailable and silent; it does not mean clean air. Mean and normalized mean remain separate diagnostics.
Image-derived qualitative PM2.5 signal. Comparisons with GEOS-CF improve regional ordering, but individual reversals and missing colors remain possible. Absolute concentrations are not validated.
messages.A comparison of visual indices 0 and 1,: A comparison of visual indices 0 and 1, not concentration measurements or the current frame. The higher index produces a higher, brighter metallic tone at the same loudness. The legend pauses playback.
messages.Less visible PM2.5 signal means a lower,: Less visible PM2.5 signal means a lower, darker tone. More visible signal means a higher, brighter tone. This index is not a concentration or health-risk rating.
messages.Sustained metallic FM tone · gentle pitc: Sustained metallic FM tone · gentle pitch glide · variable spectral brightness
messages.The supplied log-scaled position moves a: The supplied log-scaled position moves a soft metallic tone higher and brighter as PM2.5 concentration rises. The note glides with the player instead of striking on every frame. Loudness stays fixed. This is a sound code, not a health assessment or a literal sound of particles.
messages.The supplied 0–1 log-scale position cont: The supplied 0–1 log-scale position controls a fixed, monotonic pitch-and-brightness curve. During playback one sustained voice glides between frames; it adds no beat and does not retrigger on each frame.
messages.PM2.5 is an image-derived near-surface c: PM2.5 is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in µg/m³. The sound uses the supplied logarithmic legend position. Its metallic shimmer is a metaphor, not a measurement of particle size, wind or health risk.
messages.The provided norm follows the logarithmi: The provided norm follows the logarithmic 0.4–409.6 µg/m³ legend. A fixed curve, brightness = norm + 0.3 × sin(π × norm), sets a low-pass cutoff from 1400 to 6200 Hz and a continuous tone from C4 to C6. The curve is shared by the global image and every region; the front end does not recompute norm. Loudness stays fixed. Missing values or zero pixel coverage release the voice.
messages.Image-derived PM2.5 estimate, not a dire: Image-derived PM2.5 estimate, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF grid or health assessment. A higher, brighter tone means a higher supplied concentration position, not a danger rating.
messages.A comparison of 0.4 and 409.6 µg/m³ refe: A comparison of 0.4 and 409.6 µg/m³ reference values, not the current frame. Higher log-scaled PM2.5 position means a higher, brighter metallic tone at the same loudness. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on.
messages.Lower PM2.5 legend position means a lowe: Lower PM2.5 legend position means a lower, darker metallic tone. Higher position means a higher, brighter tone at the same loudness. This is not a health-risk rating.
messages.Tuned drum · C pentatonic · crisp stick: Tuned drum · C pentatonic · crisp stick attack
messages.More supplied precipitation in millimete: More supplied precipitation in millimeters produces more crisp drum strokes per second. The drum also rises through C pentatonic notes as the amount grows, so short comparisons remain audible. Every place uses the same fixed scale.
messages.Zero amount is silent. Positive amounts: Zero amount is silent. Positive amounts map to 0.5–5 coded drum strokes per second. These are musical symbols, not recorded raindrops or measured rainfall intensity.
messages.The supplied amount is in millimeters, n: The supplied amount is in millimeters, not millimeters per hour. Its accumulation interval is not stated in this JSON. The visualization includes total precipitation, including rain and snow. The mean uses color-filtered pixels only, not the whole Earth.
messages.Sound uses mean amount a in mm directly:: Sound uses mean amount a in mm directly: zero is silent; positive amounts use a fixed curve through 0.25 mm → 0.8, 0.5 mm → 1.5, 0.75 mm → 3, 1 mm → 4 and 2 mm → 4.7 strokes/s, approaching 5 for larger amounts. Drum pitch follows this same curve from C3 to C5. The normalized value remains as supplied. Missing amount or zero pixel coverage produces silence.
messages.A comparison of 0.5 mm and 1 mm referenc: A comparison of 0.5 mm and 1 mm reference amounts, not the current frame. Higher amount means faster, higher drum strokes. The legend pauses playback.
messages.Lower precipitation amount means slower,: Lower precipitation amount means slower, lower drum strokes. Higher amount means faster, higher drum strokes. These are millimeters, not millimeters per hour.
messages.Fixed C3 ensemble · sustained strings ·: Fixed C3 ensemble · sustained strings · variable harmonics
messages.Higher supplied specific humidity opens: Higher supplied specific humidity opens the harmonics of a sustained string-like pad, from dark and thin to bright and rich. Its C3 pitch and gentle detuning stay fixed.
messages.Specific humidity controls nominal filte: Specific humidity controls nominal filter bandwidth from 160 to 1600 Hz. This is a sound parameter, not a second humidity unit or a pitch mapping.
messages.Specific humidity is supplied in grams o: Specific humidity is supplied in grams of water vapor per kilogram of air, not relative humidity in percent. Values are estimated from color-filtered pixels. Image-pixel coverage is not the proportion of Earth's area with high humidity.
messages.For supplied mean specific humidity q in: For supplied mean specific humidity q in g/kg, nominal bandwidth = 160 + 1440 × (1 − exp(−q / 12)) Hz. The pad also opens a low-pass filter with cutoff 180 × 20^((bandwidth − 160) / 1440) Hz to reveal string harmonics, with gain compensation. This fixed expressive transfer is shared by frames and the legend. The provided norm is not recalculated. Missing values or zero pixel coverage produce silence.
messages.Image-derived specific-humidity estimate: Image-derived specific-humidity estimate in g/kg. This is not a direct GEOS-FP numerical field or a relative-humidity percentage. High specific humidity does not by itself imply precipitation.
messages.A comparison of 0 g/kg and 22 g/kg refer: A comparison of 0 g/kg and 22 g/kg reference values at the visualization scale endpoints, not the current frame. Higher specific humidity means richer string harmonics. The legend pauses playback.
messages.Lower specific humidity means dark, thin: Lower specific humidity means dark, thin strings. Higher specific humidity means brighter, richer strings, not rainfall.
messages.Fixed C5 · intensity and extent of visib: Fixed C5 · intensity and extent of visible wind colors
messages.Stronger and more extensive detected win: Stronger and more extensive detected wind colors produce faster pulses. The visual signal index is a qualitative image measure, not average wind speed in m/s.
messages.The same fixed visual index and 0.3–4 Hz: The same fixed visual index and 0.3–4 Hz transfer apply to every country, group and frame. Values are not stretched separately per region.
messages.The visual index combines the intensity: The visual index combines the intensity of accepted colors with their latitude-weighted extent. The conditional mean in m/s is shown only as a diagnostic. Transparent areas are unknown wind, not measured calm. No accepted pixels means unavailable, not zero wind.
messages.Python computes visualSignal = sum(area: Python computes visualSignal = sum(area weight × accepted pixel's position on the wind legend) / sum(analyzed area weights). Mean and norm retain their original meanings separately. Pulse rate = 0.3 + 3.7 × (1 − exp(−visualSignal / 0.04)) Hz.
messages.Qualitative image-derived wind signal. T: Qualitative image-derived wind signal. Transparency and the basemap still hide some winds. A three-instant comparison improved country ordering versus the old conditional mean; it does not validate every country or time. Silence for missing values does not mean no wind.
messages.A comparison of visual indices 0.01 and: A comparison of visual indices 0.01 and 0.10, not current measurements or m/s. The legend pauses playback.
messages.More intense and extensive visible wind: More intense and extensive visible wind colors mean faster pulses. This index is not physical wind speed. Missing colors do not prove calm wind.
messages.Fixed C5 · soft breath · rounded musical: Fixed C5 · soft breath · rounded musical pulses
messages.Higher supplied mean wind speed makes an: Higher supplied mean wind speed makes an airy flute-like tone pulse faster. Pitch stays at C5; pulse rate, not melody or loudness, carries wind speed.
messages.Speed maps monotonically to 0.3–4 musica: Speed maps monotonically to 0.3–4 musical pulses per second (Hz). A fixed C5 carrier adds tone; it does not encode wind speed. These pulses are a sound code, not measured gusts.
messages.This is an image-derived estimate of nea: This is an image-derived estimate of near-surface wind speed at about 10 meters. The mean uses only color-filtered pixels, not the whole Earth. Coverage is a fraction of analyzed image pixels, not a fraction of Earth's surface area. No wind direction is encoded.
messages.The supplied normalized value is shown f: The supplied normalized value is shown for reference. The sound uses mean speed in m/s directly: rate = 0.3 + 3.7 × (1 − exp(−speed / 12)) Hz. Missing speed or zero valid-pixel coverage produces silence. Small speed changes can sound very similar.
messages.Image-derived wind estimate. Transparent: Image-derived wind estimate. Transparent low speeds and overlap with the basemap exclude many pixels. This is not a full global mean or a direct numerical GEOS-FP field. Comparison with GEOS-FP remains pending.
messages.A comparison of 5 m/s and 25 m/s example: A comparison of 5 m/s and 25 m/s examples, not the current frame. Higher speed means faster musical pulses. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on.
messages.Lower wind speed means slower musical pu: Lower wind speed means slower musical pulses. Higher wind speed means faster musical pulses.
messages.Rounded harmonics · one voice · optional: Rounded harmonics · one voice · optional light ambience
messages.Lower normalized temperatures become low: Lower normalized temperatures become lower notes. Higher values become higher notes. The melody follows the supplied values without adding dramatic events.
messages.The 11 notes follow a C major pentatonic: The 11 notes follow a C major pentatonic scale across two octaves. Different values can share a note; no artificial melody is added. One temperature voice plays at a time.
messages.The image-pixel mean temperature sets on: The image-pixel mean temperature sets one note for the selected frame and region. The current mean method is explained below; area weighting still applies only to decoded pixels used. These weather values are not historical climate anomalies; a higher note is not a danger rating.
messages.The supplied normalized value ranges fro: The supplied normalized value ranges from 0 to 1. Zero maps to C3; one maps to C5. Intermediate values select the nearest step in the 11-note scale. The front end does not recalculate this value. It is not a percentage of the Earth.
messages.A narrated low-to-high pitch comparison: A narrated low-to-high pitch comparison using reference values 0 and 1, not the current frame. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on.
messages.Lower temperature values mean lower pitc: Lower temperature values mean lower pitch. Higher temperature values mean higher pitch.
messages.Example 0.5 mm — slower, lower drum stro: Example 0.5 mm — slower, lower drum strokes.
messages.Example 1 mm — faster, higher drum strok: Example 1 mm — faster, higher drum strokes.
Example 0 g/kg — dark, thin string pad.
messages.Example 22 g/kg — bright, rich string pa: Example 22 g/kg — bright, rich string pad.
messages.Visual PM2.5 index 0 — lower, darker sus: Visual PM2.5 index 0 — lower, darker sustained tone (C4).
messages.Visual PM2.5 index 1 — higher, brighter: Visual PM2.5 index 1 — higher, brighter sustained tone (C6).
messages.Example 0.4 µg/m³ — lower, darker sustai: Example 0.4 µg/m³ — lower, darker sustained tone (C4).
messages.Example 409.6 µg/m³ — higher, brighter s: Example 409.6 µg/m³ — higher, brighter sustained tone (C6).
messages.Higher normalized temperature means high: Higher normalized temperature means higher pitch
messages.More intense and extensive visible wind: More intense and extensive visible wind colors mean faster pulses; this is not a wind-speed measurement
messages.Higher wind speed means faster musical p: Higher wind speed means faster musical pulses
messages.Higher precipitation amount means faster: Higher precipitation amount means faster, higher drum strokes, not millimeters per hour

messages.Without a regional selection, readings s: Without a regional selection, readings summarize decoded pixels across the image. Select a region or country to focus the map and switch both readings and sound to that region. Pixel inclusion shows the share of analyzed image pixels used, not accuracy or geographic surface area
messages.Python converts image colors to the near: Python converts image colors to the nearest value in the visualization legend. Logos and timestamps are excluded. Regional estimates use pixel centers inside the selected boundaries; country groups follow whole-country assignments and contain land territories, not surrounding oceans. Europe includes all Russia; Asia excludes Russia
messages.P90 is the unweighted 90th percentile of: P90 is the unweighted 90th percentile of decoded pixel values, not a confidence level. These remain image-derived estimates; weighting cannot reconstruct missing or rejected pixels and does not make them direct numerical GEOS-FP fields
messages.Pixel inclusion = pixels used ÷ analyzed: Pixel inclusion = pixels used ÷ analyzed pixels after excluding overlays. It does not measure scientific accuracy, instrument reliability or geographic surface area. Missing inclusion is unavailable, not zero; 100% inclusion does not establish accuracy
messages.Python computes norm = (mean − legend mi: Python computes norm = (mean − legend minimum) ÷ (legend maximum − legend minimum), limited to 0–1 and rounded to three decimals. It is a position on the fixed legend scale, not a percentile or a percentage of Earth. The front displays the supplied values. Temperature, carbon monoxide and ozone use their supplied normalized positions for pitch. Wind and PM2.5 use the supplied visual signal index when declared. Precipitation and specific humidity use the supplied mean in their physical units
messages.Groups follow whole-country assignments,: Groups follow whole-country assignments, not physical continental boundaries. Europe includes all of Russia; Asia excludes Russia. Oceanic island territories cover land only
messages.Use your screen reader’s table commands: Use your screen reader’s table commands to explore cells. With spoken navigation, use Read this frame to hear only the highlighted frame
messages.Frame readings summarize image-derived p: Frame readings summarize image-derived pixels. Coverage is the share of analyzed image pixels used, not geographic area or accuracy. Choosing a region changes the reading and sound
messages.Mean = sum(decoded value × cosine latitu: Mean = sum(decoded value × cosine latitude) ÷ sum(cosine latitude), using accepted pixels only. P90 remains an unweighted pixel percentile. Pixel inclusion remains a pixel-count ratio, not an area percentage
messages.This dataset uses equal weights per deco: This dataset uses equal weights per decoded pixel. P90 and coverage retain their supplied definitions
This dataset uses equal weights per decoded pixel. Its mean has not been area-weighted
messages.Color-filter settings unavailable; pixel: Color-filter settings unavailable; pixel inclusion does not establish measurement accuracy
messages.No color acceptance filter is configured: No color acceptance filter is configured: each analyzed pixel is assigned its nearest legend color. 100% inclusion does not mean 100% accuracy
messages.Image-derived temperature estimate decod: Image-derived temperature estimate decoded from visualization pixels. This is not a direct numerical GEOS-FP field or a complete global field. Small variations can remain on the same pentatonic note
messages.Image-derived precipitation estimate. Co: Image-derived precipitation estimate. Colored precipitation overlays clouds and the basemap; only color-filtered pixels contribute. Coverage is the analyzed image-pixel share, not the land area receiving rain. No whole-Earth average or mm/hour conversion is assumed
messages.The supplied normalized concentration se: The supplied normalized concentration selects one note from a fixed C major pentatonic scale. Lower values sound lower; higher values sound higher. This synthetic trumpet-like tone is a data cue, not a risk alarm
messages.Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 positio: Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 position on the fixed 40–500 ppbv legend. The selected note is not stretched to the values observed in the current frames or region
messages.Carbon monoxide is an image-derived near: Carbon monoxide is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in ppbv, decoded from NASA SVS 5153 colors. It is not the raw numerical GEOS-CF grid. Global means change little in this interval; country and continent estimates vary more. Regional means currently use equal weights per accepted image pixel
messages.The supplied norm selects one of 11 C ma: The supplied norm selects one of 11 C major pentatonic notes from C3 to C5. The front end does not recompute norm. Missing norm or zero pixel coverage means silence
messages.CO values are image-derived estimates, n: CO values are image-derived estimates, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF field. Coverage is the share of analyzed image pixels used, not accuracy or geographic area. The synthetic voice does not assess health risk
messages.A comparison of 40 and 500 ppbv legend e: A comparison of 40 and 500 ppbv legend endpoints, not the current measurements. Higher supplied concentration maps to higher pitch. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on
messages.Lower carbon monoxide concentration mean: Lower carbon monoxide concentration means a lower trumpet-like note. Higher concentration means a higher note. This sound is not a health-risk rating
messages.The supplied normalized concentration se: The supplied normalized concentration selects one note from a fixed C major pentatonic scale. Ozone uses a higher register than the other melodic voices; higher values sound higher
messages.Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 positio: Each frame uses the supplied 0–1 position on the fixed 5–60 ppbv legend. The selected note is not stretched to the values observed in the current frames or region
messages.Ozone is an image-derived near-surface c: Ozone is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in ppbv, decoded from NASA SVS 5152 colors. It is not the raw numerical GEOS-CF grid. The global mean changes little in this interval; regional estimates vary more. Regional means currently use equal weights per accepted image pixel
messages.The supplied norm selects one of 11 C ma: The supplied norm selects one of 11 C major pentatonic notes from C4 to C6. The front end does not recompute norm. Missing norm or zero pixel coverage means silence
messages.Ozone values are image-derived estimates: Ozone values are image-derived estimates, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF field. About 43–46% of analyzed pixels are used in the current frames; this is image-pixel coverage, not accuracy or geographic area. The sound is not a health-risk rating
messages.A comparison of 5 and 60 ppbv legend end: A comparison of 5 and 60 ppbv legend endpoints, not the current measurements. Higher supplied concentration maps to higher pitch. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on
messages.Lower ozone concentration means a lower: Lower ozone concentration means a lower plucked note. Higher concentration means a higher note. This sound is not a health-risk rating
messages.This dataset is available for visual pla: This dataset is available for visual playback. A dedicated sound identity has not been assigned yet; it does not use the temperature instrument
messages.The normalized value is shown as supplie: The normalized value is shown as supplied. No note or pulse rate is inferred for this experience
messages.Read the selected dataset's measure, uni: Read the selected dataset's measure, unit and timestamp below the image. Values are derived from visualization pixels and are not automatically whole-Earth averages. Coverage describes color-filtered image pixels
messages.The normalized value and its limits come: The normalized value and its limits come from the dataset. No sonification has been implemented for this quantity yet
messages.Image-derived values. Use the stated dat: Image-derived values. Use the stated dataset measure and pixel coverage; no whole-Earth average or new sound mapping is assumed
messages.Sound examples are not available for thi: Sound examples are not available for this record yet
messages.This experience is visual only. Its dedi: This experience is visual only. Its dedicated sound mapping is not implemented yet
More intense and extensive detected PM2.5 colors produce a higher, brighter metallic tone. A rising tone follows an increase in visible signal; a falling tone follows a decrease. Loudness stays fixed
messages.The same 0–1 visual index and pitch curv: The same 0–1 visual index and pitch curve apply to every country, group and frame. Regions are not stretched separately: their tones can be compared directly
messages.The visual index combines log-scaled col: The visual index combines log-scaled color intensity with its area-weighted extent. It supports comparisons of more versus less signal. The concentration mean in µg/m³ remains a separate diagnostic; the index is not a concentration or health rating
messages.Sound uses the supplied visual index dir: Sound uses the supplied visual index directly. Higher indices always produce higher, brighter sustained tones on the same fixed curve. No detected pixels means unavailable and silent; it does not mean clean air. Mean and normalized mean remain separate diagnostics
Image-derived qualitative PM2.5 signal. Comparisons with GEOS-CF improve regional ordering, but individual reversals and missing colors remain possible. Absolute concentrations are not validated
messages.A comparison of visual indices 0 and 1,: A comparison of visual indices 0 and 1, not concentration measurements or the current frame. The higher index produces a higher, brighter metallic tone at the same loudness. The legend pauses playback
messages.Less visible PM2.5 signal means a lower,: Less visible PM2.5 signal means a lower, darker tone. More visible signal means a higher, brighter tone. This index is not a concentration or health-risk rating
messages.The supplied log-scaled position moves a: The supplied log-scaled position moves a soft metallic tone higher and brighter as PM2.5 concentration rises. The note glides with the player instead of striking on every frame. Loudness stays fixed. This is a sound code, not a health assessment or a literal sound of particles
messages.The supplied 0–1 log-scale position cont: The supplied 0–1 log-scale position controls a fixed, monotonic pitch-and-brightness curve. During playback one sustained voice glides between frames; it adds no beat and does not retrigger on each frame
messages.PM2.5 is an image-derived near-surface c: PM2.5 is an image-derived near-surface concentration estimate in µg/m³. The sound uses the supplied logarithmic legend position. Its metallic shimmer is a metaphor, not a measurement of particle size, wind or health risk
messages.The provided norm follows the logarithmi: The provided norm follows the logarithmic 0.4–409.6 µg/m³ legend. A fixed curve, brightness = norm + 0.3 × sin(π × norm), sets a low-pass cutoff from 1400 to 6200 Hz and a continuous tone from C4 to C6. The curve is shared by the global image and every region; the front end does not recompute norm. Loudness stays fixed. Missing values or zero pixel coverage release the voice
messages.Image-derived PM2.5 estimate, not a dire: Image-derived PM2.5 estimate, not a direct numerical GEOS-CF grid or health assessment. A higher, brighter tone means a higher supplied concentration position, not a danger rating
messages.A comparison of 0.4 and 409.6 µg/m³ refe: A comparison of 0.4 and 409.6 µg/m³ reference values, not the current frame. Higher log-scaled PM2.5 position means a higher, brighter metallic tone at the same loudness. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on
messages.Lower PM2.5 legend position means a lowe: Lower PM2.5 legend position means a lower, darker metallic tone. Higher position means a higher, brighter tone at the same loudness. This is not a health-risk rating
messages.More supplied precipitation in millimete: More supplied precipitation in millimeters produces more crisp drum strokes per second. The drum also rises through C pentatonic notes as the amount grows, so short comparisons remain audible. Every place uses the same fixed scale
messages.Zero amount is silent. Positive amounts: Zero amount is silent. Positive amounts map to 0.5–5 coded drum strokes per second. These are musical symbols, not recorded raindrops or measured rainfall intensity
messages.The supplied amount is in millimeters, n: The supplied amount is in millimeters, not millimeters per hour. Its accumulation interval is not stated in this JSON. The visualization includes total precipitation, including rain and snow. The mean uses color-filtered pixels only, not the whole Earth
messages.Sound uses mean amount a in mm directly:: Sound uses mean amount a in mm directly: zero is silent; positive amounts use a fixed curve through 0.25 mm → 0.8, 0.5 mm → 1.5, 0.75 mm → 3, 1 mm → 4 and 2 mm → 4.7 strokes/s, approaching 5 for larger amounts. Drum pitch follows this same curve from C3 to C5. The normalized value remains as supplied. Missing amount or zero pixel coverage produces silence
messages.A comparison of 0.5 mm and 1 mm referenc: A comparison of 0.5 mm and 1 mm reference amounts, not the current frame. Higher amount means faster, higher drum strokes. The legend pauses playback
messages.Lower precipitation amount means slower,: Lower precipitation amount means slower, lower drum strokes. Higher amount means faster, higher drum strokes. These are millimeters, not millimeters per hour
messages.Higher supplied specific humidity opens: Higher supplied specific humidity opens the harmonics of a sustained string-like pad, from dark and thin to bright and rich. Its C3 pitch and gentle detuning stay fixed
messages.Specific humidity controls nominal filte: Specific humidity controls nominal filter bandwidth from 160 to 1600 Hz. This is a sound parameter, not a second humidity unit or a pitch mapping
messages.Specific humidity is supplied in grams o: Specific humidity is supplied in grams of water vapor per kilogram of air, not relative humidity in percent. Values are estimated from color-filtered pixels. Image-pixel coverage is not the proportion of Earth's area with high humidity
messages.For supplied mean specific humidity q in: For supplied mean specific humidity q in g/kg, nominal bandwidth = 160 + 1440 × (1 − exp(−q / 12)) Hz. The pad also opens a low-pass filter with cutoff 180 × 20^((bandwidth − 160) / 1440) Hz to reveal string harmonics, with gain compensation. This fixed expressive transfer is shared by frames and the legend. The provided norm is not recalculated. Missing values or zero pixel coverage produce silence
messages.Image-derived specific-humidity estimate: Image-derived specific-humidity estimate in g/kg. This is not a direct GEOS-FP numerical field or a relative-humidity percentage. High specific humidity does not by itself imply precipitation
messages.A comparison of 0 g/kg and 22 g/kg refer: A comparison of 0 g/kg and 22 g/kg reference values at the visualization scale endpoints, not the current frame. Higher specific humidity means richer string harmonics. The legend pauses playback
messages.Lower specific humidity means dark, thin: Lower specific humidity means dark, thin strings. Higher specific humidity means brighter, richer strings, not rainfall
messages.Stronger and more extensive detected win: Stronger and more extensive detected wind colors produce faster pulses. The visual signal index is a qualitative image measure, not average wind speed in m/s
messages.The same fixed visual index and 0.3–4 Hz: The same fixed visual index and 0.3–4 Hz transfer apply to every country, group and frame. Values are not stretched separately per region
messages.The visual index combines the intensity: The visual index combines the intensity of accepted colors with their latitude-weighted extent. The conditional mean in m/s is shown only as a diagnostic. Transparent areas are unknown wind, not measured calm. No accepted pixels means unavailable, not zero wind
messages.Python computes visualSignal = sum(area: Python computes visualSignal = sum(area weight × accepted pixel's position on the wind legend) / sum(analyzed area weights). Mean and norm retain their original meanings separately. Pulse rate = 0.3 + 3.7 × (1 − exp(−visualSignal / 0.04)) Hz
messages.Qualitative image-derived wind signal. T: Qualitative image-derived wind signal. Transparency and the basemap still hide some winds. A three-instant comparison improved country ordering versus the old conditional mean; it does not validate every country or time. Silence for missing values does not mean no wind
messages.A comparison of visual indices 0.01 and: A comparison of visual indices 0.01 and 0.10, not current measurements or m/s. The legend pauses playback
messages.More intense and extensive visible wind: More intense and extensive visible wind colors mean faster pulses. This index is not physical wind speed. Missing colors do not prove calm wind
messages.Higher supplied mean wind speed makes an: Higher supplied mean wind speed makes an airy flute-like tone pulse faster. Pitch stays at C5; pulse rate, not melody or loudness, carries wind speed
messages.Speed maps monotonically to 0.3–4 musica: Speed maps monotonically to 0.3–4 musical pulses per second (Hz). A fixed C5 carrier adds tone; it does not encode wind speed. These pulses are a sound code, not measured gusts
messages.This is an image-derived estimate of nea: This is an image-derived estimate of near-surface wind speed at about 10 meters. The mean uses only color-filtered pixels, not the whole Earth. Coverage is a fraction of analyzed image pixels, not a fraction of Earth's surface area. No wind direction is encoded
messages.The supplied normalized value is shown f: The supplied normalized value is shown for reference. The sound uses mean speed in m/s directly: rate = 0.3 + 3.7 × (1 − exp(−speed / 12)) Hz. Missing speed or zero valid-pixel coverage produces silence. Small speed changes can sound very similar
messages.Image-derived wind estimate. Transparent: Image-derived wind estimate. Transparent low speeds and overlap with the basemap exclude many pixels. This is not a full global mean or a direct numerical GEOS-FP field. Comparison with GEOS-FP remains pending
messages.A comparison of 5 m/s and 25 m/s example: A comparison of 5 m/s and 25 m/s examples, not the current frame. Higher speed means faster musical pulses. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on
messages.Lower wind speed means slower musical pu: Lower wind speed means slower musical pulses. Higher wind speed means faster musical pulses
messages.Lower normalized temperatures become low: Lower normalized temperatures become lower notes. Higher values become higher notes. The melody follows the supplied values without adding dramatic events
messages.The 11 notes follow a C major pentatonic: The 11 notes follow a C major pentatonic scale across two octaves. Different values can share a note; no artificial melody is added. One temperature voice plays at a time
messages.The image-pixel mean temperature sets on: The image-pixel mean temperature sets one note for the selected frame and region. The current mean method is explained below; area weighting still applies only to decoded pixels used. These weather values are not historical climate anomalies; a higher note is not a danger rating
messages.The supplied normalized value ranges fro: The supplied normalized value ranges from 0 to 1. Zero maps to C3; one maps to C5. Intermediate values select the nearest step in the 11-note scale. The front end does not recalculate this value. It is not a percentage of the Earth
messages.A narrated low-to-high pitch comparison: A narrated low-to-high pitch comparison using reference values 0 and 1, not the current frame. The legend pauses the player. Labels are spoken only when spoken navigation is on
messages.Lower temperature values mean lower pitc: Lower temperature values mean lower pitch. Higher temperature values mean higher pitch
